issues.description: Attribute 'numberOfInscribedStudents' has conflicting types: the problem statement UML declares numberOfInscribedStudents as int (problem_statement.md line 65), while the solution implementation declares the field as long (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 7), uses long in the constructor parameter (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13) and exposes a getter returning long (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 30). This also leads to a compilation problem in the solution: getTotalNumberOfStudents() is declared to return int (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 75) but returns the sum of a long and an int, causing a type mismatch. The inconsistency between the UML and the implementation will confuse students about the expected type and can break compilation or automated tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of numberOfInscribedStudents consistent across the artifacts. Option A (preferred for minimal changes to the problem statement): change the solution to use int everywhere — update the field to 'private int numberOfInscribedStudents;', change the constructor parameter and getter/setter to int, and keep getTotalNumberOfStudents() returning int. Option B: if large counts are intended, update the problem statement UML and all method signatures to use long — change the UML line to long, change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long, and update any arithmetic/return sites accordingly. After choosing one option, update the constructor, field, getter, setter, and getTotalNumberOfStudents() implementation so types align and the code compiles.
